sections.h2: What should a seller know about Laurens County, Georgia property tax?
sections.html:
Laurens County sits in central Georgia, and its county offices are in Dublin. A seller here deals with two county offices: the tax commissioner, who bills and collects, and the board of tax assessors, who sets the value. Knowing which one answers which question saves a lot of phone calls before a closing.

The Census Bureau QuickFacts table lists 51,041 residents for July 2025 across 807.34 square miles of land, which works out to 61.4 people per square mile in 2020. That is the largest land area among the four Georgia counties in the same comparison, so a parcel can be a town lot in Dublin or a tract of farm and timber ground. The same table shows a median owner-occupied home value of $154,500 for 2020 to 2024, with 64.3 percent of housing units owner-occupied. Builders took out 102 permits in 2025.

Retail sales in the county reached about $1.06 billion in 2022, and health care and social assistance receipts came to $598.6 million. Median household income is $55,010 and 20.3 percent of residents are in poverty. For a seller, that points to many buyers who are first-time or budget-conscious, and a clear tax picture helps a sale move.

sections.h2: Who do I call about a Laurens County property tax bill or a value?
sections.html:
Call the tax commissioner about a bill and the assessor about a value. The county's own FAQ draws the line this way: the commissioner handles billing and collection of real property, personal property, motor vehicle, mobile home and timber tax, and the assessors answer questions about property values.

Laurens County property tax contacts as printed on county pages
OfficeWherePhone
Tax Commissioner121 E Jackson Street, Suite B, Dublin, GA 31021 (mail: P.O. Box 2099, Dublin, GA 31040)478-272-6994
Tax AssessorListed in the county staff directory478-272-6443

The commissioner's hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. The commissioner page adds that the property department also processes homestead applications, runs tax sales and sends the yearly digest to the Department of Revenue. Millage rates come from yet another group. Per the county tax FAQ, the county commissioners, the county school board, the Dublin school board and individual cities each set their own.

sections.h2: When are Laurens County property taxes due and what happens if they are late?
sections.html:
The county pages do not print a fixed calendar date, so read the due date on your bill. The Georgia Department of Revenue says taxes are normally due December 20 in most counties, some counties set another date, and taxpayers get 60 days from the billing date before the bill is late.

What the county itself says about a bill that stays unpaid:

  • More than 30 days past the due date, a tax fifa (a lien) can be recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court.
  • Those records are public, so credit bureaus can see them, and the tax office has no control over how they use them.
  • Mobile and modular homes are taxed as personal property with an April 1 due date, and the location permit is issued only after the current year's tax is paid in full.

If you are selling a house with an open bill, ask the commissioner's office for a payoff figure early. A recorded fifa on the Dublin courthouse record can slow a title search, so clearing it before you list keeps the closing on schedule.

sections.h2: How does Laurens County value a home, and how long do I have to appeal?
sections.html:
You have 45 days from the date on the assessment notice to appeal. The Board of Assessors values property as of January 1, and assessed value is 40 percent of fair market value. Millage is then applied to the net value after exemptions, and one mill means one dollar for each $1,000 of assessed value.

Every owner may file a return between January 2 and April 1 stating what they think the property is worth. The county says an initial return renews itself each year at the last value finally set, so you only file again when you add property, make improvements or want to declare a different figure. A new return also protects your appeal rights if the assessors change the number again.

The appeal itself starts in writing with the Board of Tax Assessors on the state's uniform form, and you must choose a path when you file:

  • Board of Equalization, which hears the case after the assessors have looked again. Superior Court is the next step after that.
  • Hearing officer, available only for non-homestead real property valued above $750,000.
  • Arbitration, which uses a certified appraisal from you. The arbitrator's decision is final.

Call 478-272-6443 and ask for the appeal form. The size of the tax bill is not a reason the board can act on; the grounds are taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and special assessments can Laurens County owners claim?
sections.html:
The main one is the homestead exemption, and the filing deadline is April 1. You must own and live in the home on January 1, and a late application turns on the exemption for the following year. Once approved it renews on its own until you move, change ownership or apply for a different type.

The county's information page sets out these additional programs:

  • An extra exemption at age 62, plus an exemption from the state portion of the tax at age 65 for the home and up to 10 acres when you already qualify for another homestead exemption.
  • A tax deferral for qualified homeowners age 62 and older with low household income, which postpones payment until ownership changes or the deferred amount reaches a set share of the home's value. Ask the commissioner for the current income limit.
  • Agricultural assessment at 30 percent instead of 40 percent, and Conservation Use, both with 10 year covenants.
  • Forest Land Protection, a 15 year covenant for tracts above 200 acres.

Applications for the land programs go to the Tax Assessors between January 1 and April 1. The two county pages differ on whether the commissioner or the assessor takes the homestead form, so ask either office where to bring yours. Anyone selling land enrolled in a covenant program should ask the assessors what happens to the covenant when ownership changes.

sections.h2: How does a sale in Laurens County affect who owes the tax?
sections.html:
Whoever owns the property on January 1 owes that year's bill, even if the house sells on January 2. The Department of Revenue says Georgia law gives no refund to a partial-year resident, so any sharing of the bill happens in your contract and at the closing table.

A practical order of steps for a Laurens County seller:

  • Ask the commissioner whether this year's bill has been issued and whether it is paid.
  • Have your closing attorney split the year between you and the buyer.
  • Tell the buyer to apply for their own homestead exemption by April 1 of the first year they own and live in the house.
  • If you hold an exemption, expect it to end with the sale, since a move or ownership change requires a new application.

Deeds are kept in the deed room of the Clerk of Superior Court inside the Laurens County Courthouse, which is also where a copy of your warranty deed comes from.

faqs.q: Who sets property values in Laurens County?
faqs.a: The Laurens County Board of Tax Assessors sets values. The tax commissioner only bills and collects. Call 478-272-6443 for a value question and 478-272-6994 for a bill.

faqs.q: What is the assessed value of a house in Laurens County?
faqs.a: It is 40 percent of fair market value, as of January 1. The exemption is subtracted from that figure and the millage rate is applied to what remains.

faqs.q: Is there a deadline to apply for a Laurens County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Yes, April 1. The application must be in by that date to count for the current year, and you must own and occupy the home on January 1.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Laurens County assessment after the 45 days pass?
faqs.a: No ordinary appeal is open once the 45 days from the notice date have run. Keep the notice, mark the date and call the assessors early in the window.

faqs.q: Do I need to pay a Laurens County mobile home tax before I move it?
faqs.a: Yes. Mobile and modular homes are taxed as personal property, due April 1, and the county will not issue the location permit until the current year's tax is paid in full.
